toc.title: Retrieval Matched to Data and Query

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. BM25: Best Matching 25, a keyword ranking function; LLM: large language model; PII: personally identifiable information

  • How to match retrieval to the data shape and the query pattern
  • The accuracy, latency and cost trade-off and how to justify a configuration
  • Observability at scale: what to log, trace and measure, and how to sample

2Retrieval Matched to Data and Query

Running case

Lumen Advisory Designs Search for a Retailer's Three Data Sets

  • Product manuals (long prose), order records (tables), and a code repository for the support tooling team
  • Questions range from "how do I reset the ice maker?" to "total returns last quarter for store 12" to "where is the refund rule implemented?"

Data shape Query pattern Retrieval strategy
Long prose (manuals, policies) Natural-language questions Hybrid vector plus BM25, rerank, structure-aware chunks, citations
Identifiers and exact terms Lookup by code, name, clause Keyword/BM25 or metadata filter
Structured tables Aggregation, filters, joins Query the database (text-to-SQL or a parameterized tool), not vector search
Code Find definitions and usages Agentic search with grep/glob and file reads, or a code-embedding index
Relationships (org charts, dependencies) Multi-hop Graph queries or iterative retrieval across hops
Time-sensitive data "Latest" Metadata filters and recency weighting; freshness checks
Small fixed corpus Any Full context with caching
Query pattern Technique
Direct lookup Keyword or metadata filter
Vague or short Query rewriting or expansion by the model
Multi-part or multi-hop Decompose, retrieve per part, then combine (agentic retrieval)
Needs breadth then precision Retrieve wide, rerank, pass top K
Needs authoritative sourcing Retrieve with metadata (source, date) and cite
  • Do not use vector search for aggregations. Sums, counts and joins belong in SQL or an analytics tool; let the model write a validated, parameterized query or call a safe tool.
  • Agentic retrieval (the model searches iteratively) improves recall for hard questions at the price of latency and tokens; reserve it for queries that need it, and route simple lookups to a single fast search.
  • Evaluate retrieval separately (recall@k, precision, empty-result rate) from answer quality.
Exam tip

The answer follows the data shape: prose = hybrid semantic search; exact identifiers = keyword; tables = structured query; code = search tools. "Put everything in a vector store" is the distractor.

3Accuracy-Latency-Cost Trade-offs

Lever Accuracy Latency Cost
Stronger tier Up Up Up
Higher effort / thinking Up Up Up
More retrieved chunks / rerank Up (to a point) Up Up
Prompt caching Same Down Down
Streaming Same Perceived latency down (time to first token) Same
Smaller tier / lower effort Down Down Down
Routing by difficulty Held Down on average Down
Batch API Same Much higher (not interactive) Down (50%)
Parallel calls Same Down (wall-clock) Same or up
Shorter output / max_tokens Risk if cut off Down Down
  • Justify with data: measure p50 and p95 latency, time to first token, accuracy on a test set and cost per request for each configuration; choose by the client's priority (Module 1).
  • First get a prompt that works, then optimize latency; premature trimming hides what top quality looks like.
  • Use streaming for interactive UIs, batch for non-urgent bulk, caching nearly always when a prefix repeats.
  • Ask for sentence or paragraph limits rather than word counts when shortening output.

4Observability at Scale

Observability lets you understand a running system from its outputs. For LLM systems add content quality to the usual latency, errors and cost.

Signal What to capture Why
Logs Request id (the request-id header), model, prompt version, token counts, tool calls, errors, outcome Reproduce and audit
Traces Per-run spans across retrieval, model calls, tools and subagents Debug non-deterministic multi-step runs
Metrics p50/p95 latency, time to first token, error and retry rates, cache hit rate, cost per request, escalation rate Trends and alerts
Quality signals Sampled LLM-judge or human scores, thumbs, correction rates, citation validity Detect drift
Cost attribution Usage by workspace, API key, model, team Chargeback and budgets

Challenges and answers

Challenge Practice
Volume Sample detailed traces; aggregate metrics for everything
Privacy Redact PII in logs; content logging off by default and enabled narrowly; access controls and retention limits
Non-determinism Log prompt version, parameters and retrieved context so a run can be replayed
Multi-step runs Correlate with a trace id across agents and tools
Cost surprises Per-workspace keys, usage and cost APIs, budget alerts, cache-efficiency tracking
Metric cardinality Limit labels; avoid unbounded values such as user ids in metric labels
Drift Version prompts and models; compare against eval baselines after each change
  • Anthropic usage and cost reporting (Admin API or analytics API) groups by model, workspace, API key, service tier, context window, data residency and speed; data appears within about 5 minutes; admin credentials are required.
  • Claude Code can export OpenTelemetry metrics and events (cost, tokens by type, sessions, tool decisions) to your backend; it is off until enabled, prompt text is not logged by default, and admins can set it through managed settings (Module 17).
  • Alert on leading indicators: rising retry or error rates, falling cache hit rate, growing latency tail, rising escalation or thumbs-down rates.
Exam tip

At scale, the right monitoring answer combines aggregate metrics, sampled traces, redacted logs and quality sampling; logging everything with full content is both costly and a privacy risk.

Exam tip

Choose the retrieval by data shape: prose hybrid, identifiers keyword, tables structured query, code search tools.

5Exam Q&A

S1A retailer's users ask "total returns for store 12 last quarter" over a table of 40 million order rows. Which approach fits best?

  • AAsk the model to guess the figure from similar past questions
  • BLet the model call a validated, parameterized query tool and return the computed result
  • CPaste a sample of rows into the prompt and ask the model to estimate the total for the whole quarter
  • DEmbed every order row and retrieve the nearest rows to the question
Show the answer

Answer: B. Aggregations over structured data belong in a database query, not vector search.

S2A search for a specific clause number "14(b)(2)" keeps returning loosely related passages. What helps most?

  • AIncreasing the number of retrieved passages from 5 to 50
  • BRemoving the clause numbers from the index to reduce noise from the identifiers in the passages
  • CA keyword (BM25) or metadata lookup combined with the semantic search
  • DUsing a larger generation model with the same retriever
Show the answer

Answer: C. Exact identifiers such as clause numbers need lexical matching, which a keyword index adds to the semantic search.

S3A hard multi-hop question needs facts from three documents that link to each other. Which retrieval approach suits it?

  • AA single vector search with a larger top-K so that all three linked documents are surely included
  • BDecompose the question and retrieve iteratively, with the model issuing follow-up searches
  • CA single keyword search on the full question text
  • DSkip retrieval and rely on the model's training data, which already covers the three linked documents
Show the answer

Answer: B. Iterative, agentic retrieval handles multi-hop questions, at a latency cost.

S4An interactive assistant must feel responsive and cost less, and quality is acceptable. Which TWO levers fit? Select TWO.

  • ACache the stable prompt prefix
  • BRaise effort to maximum for every turn
  • CRoute every request through the Batch API
  • DStream the response so users see the first tokens quickly
  • ERetrieve 200 passages for every question
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Streaming improves perceived latency; caching lowers time and cost.

S5Latency p95 doubled after adding a reranking step, with quality up slightly. How should the architect decide?

  • AKeep reranking because quality always outranks latency
  • BCompare the gain against the latency budget and the client's priority, then tune candidate count or reranker size
  • CAdd a second reranker to restore latency
  • DRemove reranking because latency always outranks quality
Show the answer

Answer: B. Compare the measured quality gain with the latency budget and the client's priority, then tune the candidate count or reranker size.

S6A team logs the full prompt and response for every request in a regulated workflow. What is the better observability design?

  • AKeep logging everything indefinitely in a shared bucket for convenience
  • BLog only the final answer text with user names attached
  • CAggregate metrics for all traffic, sampled and redacted traces, and content logging only where needed and controlled
  • DDisable all logging to protect privacy
Show the answer

Answer: C. Aggregate metrics for all traffic plus sampled, redacted traces balance debuggability against privacy, cost and retention duties.

S7Spend for one product line is rising unexpectedly. Which setup makes the cause easiest to find?

  • AAsking developers to estimate their own usage
  • BOne shared key for all applications and a monthly invoice review by the finance team after the bill arrives
  • CSeparate workspaces or keys per application and reports grouped by model and key, with budget alerts
  • DLowering max_tokens on every application
Show the answer

Answer: C. Attribution by workspace and key enables chargeback and investigation.

S8Which metric is a leading indicator of a prompt-cache regression after a release?

  • AA rising count of user logins
  • BA rising number of documentation page views by developers
  • CA falling number of deployments
  • DA falling cache hit rate with rising input cost
Show the answer

Answer: D. A changed prefix breaks caching; the hit rate drops first.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
By shape Prose: hybrid plus rerank · identifiers: keyword · tables: structured query · code: search tools · relationships: iterative or graph
Never Vector search for sums and joins
Query rewriting For vague or short queries
Trade-offs Tier, effort, retrieval depth, rerank up = accuracy, latency, cost up; caching down; batch cheap but slow
Metrics p50 and p95 latency, time to first token, cost per request, cache hit rate, errors
Observability Logs (request id), traces, metrics, quality sampling, cost attribution
Scale Sample traces; redact PII; limit cardinality; alert on leading indicators
Reporting Usage and cost by model, workspace, key; about 5 minutes fresh
